concerns.concern: The relaxation-rate result in Fig. 2c is the paper's main argument against ordinary vortex pinning. But a ramp-speed-dependent critical current also occurs in an ordinary NbSe2 vortex lattice, so this test alone may not separate an intrinsic effect from ordinary pinning.
concerns.quote: Xiao et al. report a ramp-speed-dependent critical current in an ordinary NbSe2 vortex lattice, so that test by itself may not separate the two readings.

concerns.concern: In both samples the memory window sits next to a field range where Jc rises with field, so it could be a supercooled metastable disordered vortex phase near a peak effect. Field-cooled and zero-field-cooled states at the same field were not compared, and the paper does not say whether fields were swept at 50 mK or field cooled.
concerns.quote: Field cool S2 to 9 to 14 T and compare the first Jc with the pumped state; overlay the Jc(B) from Fig. 4b on the ΔJ window of Fig. 4e.

concerns.concern: Disorder injected at the sample edges through surface barriers could produce history-dependent critical currents. The paper argues this away rather than testing it, for example by measuring the current distribution or comparing ac and dc Jc at several frequencies in the same sample.
concerns.quote: Compare ac Jc at a few frequencies with dc Jc in S2 at 14 T; in NbSe2, edge-injected disorder makes the two differ

concerns.concern: Joule heating during the current pulses is only partly ruled out. The temperature traces are in a Supplementary Information file not included in the PDF. The thermometer location, contact resistances and power dissipated during the 40 mA reset and the pumps are not given.
concerns.quote: Put the temperature traces in the main PDF, with the thermometer's location, the contact resistances and the power during the 40 mA reset.

concerns.concern: Vortex edge barriers and Meissner screening could mimic the effect. The effect has not been followed against sample width or edge quality, and field and angle dependence is shown for S2 only.
concerns.quote: Repeat the pump and erase sequence of Fig. 2 on a crystal cut to a different width, or after re-polishing its edges.

concerns.concern: The paper does not say how many crystals were measured with the pulse protocol, how many showed the memory effect, or why any were set aside. In particular, sample S3 appears only in ac data and it is unclear whether it shows the effect.
concerns.quote: S3 appears only in the ac data of Fig. 4h, and the paper doesn't say whether S3 shows the memory effect.

concerns.concern: The memory region in S2 starts near 7 T and peaks near 10 T, while the cited coexistence region lies at about 15 to 20 T. The paper does not explain what sets the lower edge of the memory region or whether it moves with sample quality.
concerns.quote: What sets the lower edge of the memory region, and does it move with sample quality the way the upper edge does?

concerns.concern: ΔJ is read at a fixed 1 µV criterion and the memory-region boundary is defined by ΔJ reaching zero within resolution. The paper does not show how the boundaries move with other voltage criteria or excitation currents, or state the ΔJ resolution.
concerns.quote: How do the boundaries in Fig. 4e and 4f move for other voltage criteria and other Jex, and what is the ΔJ resolution?

concerns.concern: The paper does not explain how the shown datasets and fields were chosen. It also does not show second-best data, such as an S1 map of ΔJ versus B corresponding to Fig. 4e.
concerns.quote: Say how S3 behaves under the pulse protocol and how the shown fields were picked; show the S1 counterpart of Fig. 4e.

concerns.concern: Several measurement choices are not fully disclosed: rotation covers only b toward c, and the reasons for the chosen fields and the sample cross-sections used to compute J are not given. It is also unclear what was measured beyond the shown ranges, such as rotation toward a, S1 away from 20 T, excitations above 20 A cm^-2, and the waiting times behind the 'several hours' claim.
concerns.quote: Rotation covers b toward c only. The reasons behind the shown fields (7, 9, 14, 15, 20 T) and the sample cross-sections behind J aren't given.

concerns.concern: Data and code availability is incomplete. The datasets are only promised for upload before publication, and the instrument code is in a supplement.
concerns.quote: The datasets supporting the findings of this study will be uploaded to the University of Cambridge Apollo Repository prior to publication
